statement: Let $a_n$ be a sequence of positive reals with $a_n=\max_{1\leq i\leq 2025}a_{n-i}-\min_{1\leq i\leq 2025}a_{n-i}$ for $n>2025$. Prove there exists $M$ such that $a_n<\frac{1}{1404}$ for all $n>M$.

$p$ is prime. Cards labeled $0,1,\ldots,p-1$ (0 appears once, others at most once). For each pair $x,y$, determine a winner. Conditions: (a) transitivity; (b) if $x$ doesn't beat $y$ and $y$ doesn't beat $z$, then $x+z$ doesn't beat $y+t$ for any $t$. Find the maximum number of cards.

$n>10$ lines in the plane, no three concurrent, no two parallel. At least $n^2/8+1$ bounded regions are colored black. A good triangle is formed by three lines lying entirely in a black region. Prove there are at least $n/2$ good triangles.

Numbers 2 to 99 on a board. Operations: (a) erase $i$ and $i+10$ if both present ($2\leq i\leq 89$); (b) erase $i$ and $i+1$ if both present ($2\leq i\leq 98$). Find the maximum number that can be erased.

Scalene $\triangle ABC$. Incircle touches $BC$ at $D$. $T_B$, $T_C$ are the second intersections of the $B$- and $C$-angle bisectors with the circumcircle. $X_B$ is the antipode of $A$ in the circumcircle of $\triangle ACD$; $X_C$ in the circumcircle of $\triangle ABD$. Prove $\triangle BT_CX_C\sim\triangle CT_BX_B$.

Right $\triangle ABC$ ($\angle A=90^\circ$), $M$ midpoint of $BC$, $P$ on $AM$. Reflection of $BP$ over $AB$ meets $AC$ at $T$ and $AM$ at $Q$. Circumcircles of $\triangle BPQ$ and $\triangle ABC$ meet again at $F$. Prove the circumcenter of $\triangle CFT$ lies on $BQ$.

$f(x,y)$ is $n$-friendly if for fewer than 1\% of integers $|k|\leq n$, the equation $f(x,y)=k$ has a solution $(x_0,y_0)$ with $x_0\in[y_0/100,100y_0]$. Suppose $f\leq g$ where $g$ is a polynomial with real coefficients, negative leading term, total degree $>2$, and $g(x,y)\to\infty$ as $y/x\to 1$. Prove $f$ is not $n$-friendly for large $n$.

$n$ is lucky if it has $\geq 2$ distinct prime divisors and can be written as $n=p_1^{\alpha_1}+\cdots+p_k^{\alpha_k}$ where $p_1,\ldots,p_k$ are distinct primes dividing $n$. Prove for every prime $p$ there exists a lucky $n$ with $p\mid n$.

$n$ cups labeled $1,\ldots,n$ (cup $i$ has capacity $i$ liters). Total: $n$ liters in integer amounts. Transfers (source empties or destination fills). (a) Prove any integer-amount configuration reaches all-1's in at most $4n/3$ steps. (b) Prove any integer configuration reaches any other in at most $5n/3$ steps.

Scalene $\triangle ABC$. $Y,X$ on $AC,BC$ with $BC\perp XY$. $Z,T$ are reflections of $X,Y$ over midpoints of $BC,AC$. $P$ on $ZT$ such that the circumcenter of $\triangle XZP$ equals the circumcenter of $\triangle ABC$. Prove the nine-point circle of $\triangle ABC$ passes through the midpoint of $XP$.
